title: Inputs
summary: Inputs collect structured data; labels, constraints and feedback determine completion quality.

MUST.text: Associate a persistent visible label with every field; placeholders are examples, not labels.
Use native input/select/textarea with appropriate type and autocomplete; preserve paste and autofill.
Identify input errors in text and associate them with the field (aria-describedby/aria-invalid).

SHOULD.text: Show format constraints and required/optional status before submission; preserve valid data after errors.
Provide an accessible name, hint and (where needed) visible helper text adjacent to the field.

AVOID.text: Do not block paste or use placeholder-only labels.
Do not clear valid input on validation failure.

DECIDE.decision: Native input with type and label
Mark optional or omit required marker consistently
Inline message + preserve value + focus field

EXAMPLE.good: “Work email” label + hint “We send receipts here” + placeholder “name@company.com”; invalid value retained with a message
EXAMPLE.bad: placeholder-only label “Enter email” that clears on error

FAILURE_MODES: Placeholder-only labels disappear on input and fail screen readers.
Clearing valid values forces rework and abandonment.
Unannounced or color-only errors are missed by assistive-tech users.

checks.text: Errors preserve data and are announced?
